hypothesis: The production JS random-line implementation omits C signed-byte roughness conversion at the public wrapper-to-recursion boundary.
expectedBehavior: Pinned C narrows integer128/255/256 to-128/-1/0, yields the same11-cell deterministic selection with0 draws.
observedBehavior: JS yields15 painted cells and14 RNG draws for each target. Four controls0/1/7/127 match C cells and draw consumption.

witness.scope: Exact C five-number selection.randline wrapper versus exported production JS selection_randline→public des.terrain, fixed valid integer inputs/default frame, three targets/four controls.
limitations: Supported API scope: five-number C selection.randline wrapper versus exported JS selection_randline consumed by public des.terrain, the same production composition used by Bar-strt. Fixed relative endpoints20,8→30,12 and default frame1,0; C returns absolute selection cells while JS relative selection is translated by the real terrain API. No arbitrary private helper export or new Lua runtime.

C wrapper accepts positive integer roughness without an explicit range check, then its actual call converts int to schar. Config is non-AZTEC signed char,8-bit bytes,Clang19.1.7; runtime asserts CHAR_BIT8/SCHAR_MIN-128/SCHAR_MAX127. Out-of-range signed narrowing is compiler/configuration-sensitive; no universal C-implementation claim.

Three targets rough128/255/256 narrow to-128/-1/0; all yield11 C cells with0 rn2 calls. JS keeps the full integer, clamps to endpoint distance10, and produces15 cells/14 calls for the fixed seed. Controls0/1/7/127 match points and draw consumption. Do not infer arbitrary roughness/seed/frame/topology equivalence.

C executes exact l_selection_randline, recursive randline and selection allocation/copy/get/set/free bodies. Typed Lua-stack adapters accept the five integer arguments and delegate new/clone to exact C helpers. Explicit coordinate adapter asserts endpoints and frame1,0. No parser/coercion, six-argument selection-in-place form or room-coordinate claim.

Control C rn2 validates and consumes the actual JS legal draw tape. Target C consumes no RNG regardless of that tape; trailing unused input is drained only after evaluation to avoid an early-exit stdin race. This proves consumption/geometry difference, not independent RNG implementation parity.

C output is the API-returned selection set, not a complete C terrain pipeline replay. JS public terrain painting exposes those selected map cells on a STONE level; all cells are valid interior coordinates and ordinary ROOM targets, with no runtime effects or finalization.

Inspected shipped Bar-strt caller passes roughness7. Large-value shipped exposure and hidden-score relevance are unknown; this is a supported integer-API contract difference. Earlier small-roughness matching cases remain valid in their finite scopes. Three parked gaps and Main-owned candidates unchanged.

exposure.reason: Production export/composition with valid integer arguments; shipped caller inspected uses7, so large-value exposure and score impact unknown.

origin.reason: Manual source-led signed-byte parameter conversion. Frozen selection_do_randline getpoint/setpoint edge leads describe accessor naming, not this narrowing cause, and remain unreviewed; no forced scanner binding.
